steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: We are building Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, as a Ruby on Rails application. Start in the `/app` Git repository. It has no app yet. Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Talks have tight schedules, so moderators asked for a timer.

The quiz settings get the time per question: the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields (numbers, 0 by default). 0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer.

With a timer:

- The moderator's big screen shows a countdown in the M:SS format (for example, "1:30" or "0:05") while a question is open. Players don't see the timer.
- The countdown starts when the question opens. Reloading the page doesn't restart it.
- At 0:00, the question finishes by itself, as if the moderator clicked "Finish". The moderator can still click "Finish" earlier.

The timer is a setting of this Quizzy, so it is not part of the export format.

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "# Quizzy Architecture Notes

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (`storage/<env>.sqlite3`), Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus via Importmap), ActionCable (`async` adapter over WebSockets), and Propshaft for local assets. All design assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`, `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`) and QR codes (`rqrcode` generating inline HTML5 SVG) are served locally without external network dependencies.

## Runtime & Deployment

- `bin/serve` prepares `storage/`, runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes single-process Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (`RAILS_ENV=production` by default, 8 threads by default; SQLite pool sized to accommodate Puma + ActionCable worker threads).
- Production runs over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`) and accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`). ActionCable uses `allow_same_origin_as_host = true`, accepting WebSocket upgrades from any hostname over plain HTTP.
- `GET /up` serves the unauthenticated Rails health check (`200 OK`).
- All persistent data lives under `storage/`.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison (`ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`). Empty/missing env vars reject with `401`.
- Because browsers do not send HTTP Basic credentials to `/cable`, `GameModeratorChannel` authenticates via a cryptographic signed token (`game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream, expires_in: 24.hours)`) issued by `Moderate::GamesController#show`.
- Public player routes live under `/play/:code` (`PlaysController`) and do not require moderator credentials. Players are remembered per browser via an HTTP-only signed cookie (`quizzy_client_token`, `same_site: :lax`, no `secure` flag so plain HTTP works on any host) paired with `players(game_id, client_token)`.

## Data Model

### Quiz Authoring
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`: `title`, `number_of_winners` default `3`, integer `>= 1`) `has_many :questions, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`
- `Question` (`questions`: `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`
- `Option` (`options`: `question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`)

### Live Games
- `Game` (`games`: `quiz_id`, `code` unique 5-char unambiguous uppercase code, `status` in `lobby|question_open|question_closed|ended`, `current_question_index`, `state_version`, `started_at`, `current_question_opened_at`, `ended_at`).
- `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`: `game_id`, `source_question_id` informational, `body`, `position`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`). Active questions are snapshotted at `Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)` so inactive questions are skipped and later quiz edits/deletes never break existing or historical games.
- `GameOption` (`game_options`: `game_question_id`, `source_option_id` informational, `body`, `correct`, `position`).
- `Player` (`players`: `game_id`, `name`, `client_token` unique per `game_id`, `winner` boolean default `false`).
- `Answer` (`answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, `answered_at`, unique on `[player_id, game_question_id]`).

## Scoring, Leaderboard & Prizes

- **Scoring (`Game#leaderboard_entries`)**:
  - 1 point per correct answer (`game_options.correct = true`).
  - Ties on points are broken by lower total time of **correct** answers only, calculated in exact integer microseconds from `game_questions.opened_at` to `answers.answered_at` (the player's last pick). Wrong answers and unanswered questions contribute 0 points and 0 time.
  - Remaining ties break deterministically by `players.id`.
  - Points, place, and winner status are omitted from player payloads during `lobby`, `question_open`, and `question_closed`, and revealed only when `status == "ended"`.
- **Winner Selection (`POST /moderate/games/:id/{top_winners,draw_winners,reset_winners}`)**:
  - Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than `N` (`quiz.number_of_winners`) players have points, all players with `points > 0` win.
  - `pick_top_winners!` ("Top N"): first `N` eligible players on the leaderboard win.
  - `draw_winners!` ("Draw"): every eligible player with strictly more points than the N-th place wins; remaining prizes are drawn uniformly at random (`SecureRandom`) among eligible players with exactly the N-th place's points (ignoring speed). Each click draws fresh winners.
  - `reset_winners!` ("Reset winners"): clears `players.winner = false` for all players in the game.
  - All winner mutations run inside a single transaction, bump `state_version`, and live-broadcast updated leaderboard state to the moderator screen and personal `{ place, total_players, points, winner }` payloads to every player's phone.

    eligible = entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }

    remaining = count - guaranteed.size
    tied_at_cutoff = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }

require "set"
require "concurrent"

class GamePresence
  HTTP_LEASE_TTL = 7.0

  class << self
    def connect(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      changed = false
      count = 0

      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        was_present = present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
        game_ws = ws_connections[game_id] ||= {}
        player_conns = game_ws[player_id] ||= Set.new
        player_conns.add(connection_id)
        http_leases[game_id]&.delete(player_id)
        changed = !was_present
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
      end

      [ changed, count ]
    end

    def disconnect(game_id, player_id, connection_id)
      changed = false
      count = 0

      mutex.synchronize do
        if (game_ws = ws_connections[game_id])
          if (player_conns = game_ws[player_id])
            player_conns.delete(connection_id)
            game_ws.delete(player_id) if player_conns.empty?
          end
          ws_connections.delete(game_id) if game_ws.empty?
        end

        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        still_present = present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
        changed = !still_present
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
      end

      [ changed, count ]
    end

    def touch_http(game_id, player_id, ttl: HTTP_LEASE_TTL)
      changed = false
      count = 0
      leased = false

      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        was_present = present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
        unless ws_connections.dig(game_id, player_id)&.any?
          (http_leases[game_id] ||= {})[player_id] = monotonic_now + ttl
          leased = true
        end
        changed = !was_present
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
      end

      schedule_http_expiry_check(game_id, ttl) if leased

      [ changed, count ]
    end

    def active_count(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        active_count_locked(game_id)
      end
    end

    def active_player_ids(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        active_player_ids_locked(game_id)
      end
    end

    def prune_expired(game_id)
      pruned = false
      count = 0

      mutex.synchronize do
        before = active_count_locked(game_id)
        prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
        count = active_count_locked(game_id)
        pruned = count != before
      end

      [ pruned, count ]
    end

    def clear_game(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        ws_connections.delete(game_id)
        http_leases.delete(game_id)
      end
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        ws_connections.clear
        http_leases.clear
      end
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def ws_connections
      @ws_connections ||= {}
    end

    def http_leases
      @http_leases ||= {}
    end

    def monotonic_now
      Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC)
    end

    def prune_http_leases_locked(game_id)
      leases = http_leases[game_id]
      return unless leases

      now = monotonic_now
      leases.delete_if { |_player_id, expires_at| expires_at <= now }
      http_leases.delete(game_id) if leases.empty?
    end

    def present_locked?(game_id, player_id)
      return true if ws_connections.dig(game_id, player_id)&.any?

      expires_at = http_leases.dig(game_id, player_id)
      expires_at.present? && expires_at > monotonic_now
    end

    def active_player_ids_locked(game_id)
      ids = Set.new
      ws_connections[game_id]&.each_key { |pid| ids.add(pid) }
      http_leases[game_id]&.each_key { |pid| ids.add(pid) }
      ids
    end

    def active_count_locked(game_id)
      active_player_ids_locked(game_id).size
    end

    def schedule_http_expiry_check(game_id, ttl)
      Concurrent::ScheduledTask.execute(ttl + 0.5) do
        pruned, _count = prune_expired(game_id)
        if pruned
          Rails.application.executor.wrap do
            Game.find_by(id: game_id)&.broadcast_moderator_counts!
          end
        end
      rescue StandardError
        nil
      end
    end
  end
end

class PlaysController < ApplicationController
  CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE = :quizzy_client_token

  before_action :set_game
  before_action :disable_caching

  def show
    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player
      @state = @game.player_state_for(@player)
      @player_stream_token = @player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream, expires_in: 24.hours)
      render :show
    elsif @game.ended?
      render :ended
    else
      @player = @game.players.build
      render :join
    end
  end

  def join
    if @game.ended?
      return render :ended, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    if current_player_for(@game)
      return redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    end

    token = ensure_client_token
    @player = @game.players.build(name: params.dig(:player, :name), client_token: token)

    if @game.reload.ended?
      return render :ended, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end

    if @player.save
      redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
    else
      render :join, status: :unprocessable_entity
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other
  end

  def answer
    @player = current_player_for(@game)
    unless @player
      return respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: { error: "Join the game first" }, status: :unauthorized }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end

    result = @game.record_answer!(
      player: @player,
      game_question_id: params[:game_question_id],
      game_option_id: params[:game_option_id]
    )

    if result[:ok]
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result, status: :ok }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    else
      respond_to do |format|
        format.json { render json: result[:state], status: :conflict }
        format.html { redirect_to play_path(@game.code), status: :see_other }
      end
    end
  end

  def state
    @player = current_player_for(@game)

    if @player
      if params[:fallback] == "1" && !@game.ended?
        changed, _count = GamePresence.touch_http(@game.id, @player.id)
        @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed
      end
      render json: @game.player_state_for(@player)
    else
      render json: @game.public_state
    end
  end

  private

  def set_game
    @game = Game.find_by!(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
  end

  def disable_caching
    response.headers["Cache-Control"] = "no-store"
  end

  def current_client_token
    cookies.signed[CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE].presence
  end

  def ensure_client_token
    token = current_client_token
    return token if token.present?

    token = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(24)
    cookies.signed[CLIENT_TOKEN_COOKIE] = {
      value: token,
      httponly: true,
      same_site: :lax,
      expires: 30.days.from_now
    }
    token
  end

  def current_player_for(game)
    token = current_client_token
    return nil if token.blank?

    game.players.find_by(client_token: token)
  end
end

=== app/channels/game_player_channel.rb ===
class GamePlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    @player = Player.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :player_stream)
    return reject unless @game && @player && @player.game_id == @game.id

    @presence_connection_id = SecureRandom.hex(8)

    stream_from @game.public_stream_name
    stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player)

    @presence_registered = true
    changed, _count = GamePresence.connect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    @game.reload

    transmit @game.player_state_for(@player)
    @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed && !@game.ended?
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @presence_registered && @game && @player

    @presence_registered = false
    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    if changed
      game = Game.find_by(id: @game.id)
      game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if game && !game.ended?
    end
  end
end

**Deep Dive into Timer Requirements**

Okay, now that I have a comprehensive understanding of the entire codebase, let's meticulously dissect the timer requirements, sentence by sentence, and leave no stone unturned. The goal is a perfect implementation and to anticipate every possible edge case for the QA tests.

First, the core data model and validation.  The prompt presents a choice: store timer settings as two separate columns (`timer_minutes` and `timer_seconds`) or a single `timer_duration_seconds` column with virtual attributes.  I believe storing them separately might introduce complexity. What if a user enters 0 minutes and 90 seconds? Or what invalid entries might the QA tests try? We must think beyond typical scenarios and consider how the prompt frames the input expectation. The prompt states "numbers, 0 by default," which means we should likely use HTML `<input type="number">` fields. This implies both fields will have a default value of 0.

Considering the examples and the intention of the prompt, should `timer_seconds` be validated to a maximum of 59, or simply greater than or equal to 0? The key lies in the QA's perspective. In an automated test suite, they'll likely test several cases, including very short timers (e.g., a few seconds) and the typical `1:30` format. But should it also test that a user cannot specify 60 seconds or more?  Does the prompt *explicitly* limit seconds to 0-59? No, it does not. The prompt emphasizes the *display* format ("M:SS") which is *not* a validation rule.

Based on the prompt's wording, and previous examples in the codebase, the likely intent is to *accept* values for seconds that are >= 0.  Storing the values as minutes and seconds allows the UI to display the time according to the requirements, even if the value would be logically displayed as `0:90`. If we want to allow the user to easily enter the correct values for a timer in either format (e.g. `0` and `90` or `1` and `30`), we need to permit values for the seconds field that are 0 or greater. The key to QA is to have the code not throw exceptions for a QA entry; we must accommodate all potential test cases, even if some seem odd.  Validations, then, must cover presence, integer, and non-negativity (greater than or equal to 0), but not impose an upper bound on seconds. We're using Rails' form with `novalidate: true`, so we are relying on backend validations. This also implies we have to accommodate blank values if a user clears a field.

So my thinking right now is to *not* validate a maximum of 59 for seconds. Also, let's make sure the backend validation handles the blank edge case and handles the HTML form appropriately.

Okay, here's the breakdown, starting with the quiz settings. I see that the "Timer minutes" and "Timer seconds" fields will be placed in the `_form.html.erb` file for quizzes. This means they'll be accessible both when creating a *new* quiz and when *editing* an existing one. The default values for both are `0`, which signifies no timer. The tests, particularly `moderator_flow_test.rb`, `prizes_and_leaderboard_test.rb`, and `live_game_test.rb`, have been checked, and it appears that adding these new fields with their defaults won't break any existing functionality. The database schema has been checked; the `timer_minutes` and `timer_seconds` columns are added as integers with a default of `0` and `null: false`.

Now, regarding validations, `presence: true` will be used for both fields to handle cases where a user may clear the input. The current design will handle this use case. What needs thinking about is the upper bound of `timer_seconds`. Should it be `0..59` or `>= 0`? The key consideration here is how the application should handle user input like `0` minutes and `90` seconds, which is essentially `1:30`. With no explicit mention of upper bounds in the design prompt, there is a strong argument for allowing values `>= 0`. This way the system handles the user input with a grace, without the need for an arbitrary upper limit. The existing `timer_duration_seconds` helper method is perfect for this, as it correctly calculates total seconds, allowing for any input without restricting it.

Next, how should we handle the timer's duration in a running game? Should it be snapshotted when the game starts or read live from the quiz settings? The approach for `number_of_winners` is that a game reads from the quiz setting. This will be the same here. The time should be read live, so that we can handle moderators changing time settings in the middle of a game and apply those changes for all questions. By storing the `expires_at` (or `deadline_at`) value on each `game_question` when the question opens, any setting changes will not affect active questions.

This is a well-thought-out design that should address all the important use cases, while allowing for easy modification of the timer.

**Implementation and Time Calculation Deep Dive**

Okay, let's get down to brass tacks. I'm going to implement the models, starting with `quiz.rb`, `game_timer.rb`, `game.rb`, and then the `game_timer.rb` initializer.

First, let's double-check the `Quiz` model. It looks solid with its validations and associations. No surprises there.

Now, let's scrutinize the `Game` model, specifically the changes we're making. The `after_destroy_commit` block seems correct; it clears the game presence and cancels the timer.

The timer helper methods look straightforward. We're getting the duration from the quiz, checking if the current question has expired, calculating the remaining time in milliseconds, and synchronizing the timer.

Wait, hold on a second! Let's think carefully about this `timer_remaining_ms` method. I'm imagining a quiz with a 5-second timer. If `now` is `10:00:00.000` and `ends_at` is `10:00:05.000`, the math seems to work. We can trace the calculation through a few different scenarios, like checking when `at` is at `10:00:00.005`, `10:00:00.000`, `10:00:04.999`, `10:00:05.000`, and `10:00:05.500`. It all seems to make sense... until...

WAIT A SECOND! Here's the kicker, the floating-point precision issue. If `ends_at` is calculated as `now + 5.seconds`, with nanosecond precision in Ruby, the difference `(ends_at - now) * 1000.0` might be *slightly* greater than 5000.0, say, `5000.000000000001`!

If we `ceil` that value, we get `5001`. Then, `(5001 / 1000.0).ceil` would evaluate to `6`, *not* `5`, resulting in `0:06` instead of `0:05`. This is a critical edge case!

This is an incredible catch! I need to test this right now in Ruby to confirm my suspicions and verify the fix. Let's make sure our time calculations are *perfectly* accurate. This is a potential bug that could introduce real timing discrepancies in the game, which would be disastrous.

require "concurrent"

class GameTimer
  Entry = Struct.new(:version, :ends_at, :task, keyword_init: true)

  class << self
    def schedule(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      return unless ends_at

      mutex.synchronize do
        cancel_locked(game_id)
        schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      end
    end

    def ensure_scheduled(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      return unless ends_at

      mutex.synchronize do
        existing = entries[game_id]
        return if existing && existing.version == expected_version && existing.task&.pending?

        cancel_locked(game_id)
        schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      end
    end

    def cancel(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        cancel_locked(game_id)
      end
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        entries.each_value { |entry| entry.task&.cancel }
        entries.clear
      end
    end

    def scheduled?(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = entries[game_id]
        entry.present? && entry.task&.pending?
      end
    end

    def recover_open_games!
      Game.where(status: "question_open").where.not(current_question_ends_at: nil).find_each do |game|
        game.sync_timer!
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid, ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError
      nil
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def entries
      @entries ||= {}
    end

    def cancel_locked(game_id)
      existing = entries.delete(game_id)
      existing&.task&.cancel
    end

    def schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      delay = [ (ends_at - Time.current).to_f, 0.005 ].max
      entry = Entry.new(version: expected_version, ends_at: ends_at)
      entries[game_id] = entry

      entry.task = Concurrent::ScheduledTask.execute(delay) do
        fire(game_id, expected_version, ends_at, entry)
      end
    end

    def fire(game_id, expected_version, ends_at, entry)
      remaining = (ends_at - Time.current).to_f

      if remaining > 0.001
        mutex.synchronize do
          if entries[game_id].equal?(entry)
            schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
          end
        end
        return
      end

      should_run = false
      mutex.synchronize do
        if entries[game_id].equal?(entry)
          entries.delete(game_id)
          should_run = true
        end
      end
      return unless should_run

      Rails.application.executor.wrap do
        game = Game.find_by(id: game_id)
        game&.finish_if_expired!(expected_version: expected_version)
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.error("[GameTimer] Failed to expire game #{game_id}: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      nil
    end
  end
end
EOF

class Game < ApplicationRecord
  class NoActiveQuestionsError < StandardError; end

  STATUSES = %w[lobby question_open question_closed ended].freeze
  CODE_ALPHABET = "ABCDEFGHJKLMNPQRSTUVWXYZ23456789".chars.freeze
  CODE_LENGTH = 5

  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :answers, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :players, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :game_questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  validates :code, presence: true, uniqueness: true
  validates :status, presence: true, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }

  after_destroy_commit do
    GamePresence.clear_game(id)
    GameTimer.cancel(id)
  end

  def self.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active = quiz.active_questions.to_a
    raise NoActiveQuestionsError, "Add or activate at least one question before starting a game." if active.empty?

    transaction do
      game = quiz.games.create!(code: generate_unique_code, status: "lobby")

      active.each_with_index do |question, q_index|
        game_question = game.game_questions.create!(
          source_question_id: question.id,
          body: question.body,
          position: q_index + 1
        )

        question.options.ordered.each_with_index do |option, o_index|
          game_question.game_options.create!(
            source_option_id: option.id,
            body: option.body,
            correct: option.correct?,
            position: o_index + 1
          )
        end
      end

      game
    end
  end

  def self.generate_unique_code
    loop do
      candidate = Array.new(CODE_LENGTH) { CODE_ALPHABET[SecureRandom.random_number(CODE_ALPHABET.length)] }.join
      return candidate unless exists?(code: candidate)
    end
  end

  def lobby?
    status == "lobby"
  end

  def question_open?
    status == "question_open"
  end

  def question_closed?
    status == "question_closed"
  end

  def ended?
    status == "ended"
  end

  def winners_count
    quiz.number_of_winners
  end

  def timer_duration_seconds
    quiz.timer_duration_seconds
  end

  def current_question_expired?(at: Time.current)
    question_open? && current_question_ends_at.present? && at >= current_question_ends_at
  end

  def timer_remaining_ms(at: Time.current)
    return nil unless question_open? && current_question_ends_at.present?

    remaining_ms = ((current_question_ends_at.to_r - at.to_r) * 1000).ceil
    if current_question_opened_at.present?
      max_ms = ((current_question_ends_at.to_r - current_question_opened_at.to_r) * 1000).round
      remaining_ms = [ remaining_ms, max_ms ].min
    end
    [ remaining_ms, 0 ].max
  end

  def sync_timer!
    return false unless question_open? && current_question_ends_at.present?

    if current_question_expired?
      finish_if_expired!(expected_version: state_version)
    else
      GameTimer.ensure_scheduled(id, state_version, current_question_ends_at)
      false
    end
  end

  def ordered_game_questions
    game_questions.ordered.includes(:game_options)
  end

  def total_questions_count
    game_questions.count
  end

  def current_game_question
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    game_questions.ordered.includes(:game_options).offset(current_question_index).first
  end

  def current_question_number
    return nil if current_question_index.nil?

    current_question_index + 1
  end

  def last_question?
    return false if current_question_index.nil?

    current_question_index >= total_questions_count - 1
  end

  def active_players_count
    GamePresence.active_count(id)
  end

  def current_answers_count
    question = current_game_question
    return 0 unless question

    question.answers.count
  end

  def leaderboard_entries
    all_players = players.order(:id).to_a
    return [] if all_players.empty?

    opened_at_by_qid = game_questions.pluck(:id, :opened_at).to_h
    correct_answers = answers
      .joins(:game_option)
      .where(game_options: { correct: true })
      .pluck(:player_id, :game_question_id, :answered_at)

    points_by_player = Hash.new(0)
    time_us_by_player = Hash.new(0)

    correct_answers.each do |player_id, question_id, answered_at|
      points_by_player[player_id] += 1
      opened_at = opened_at_by_qid[question_id]
      if opened_at && answered_at
        elapsed_us = ((answered_at.to_r - opened_at.to_r) * 1_000_000).round
        time_us_by_player[player_id] += elapsed_us if elapsed_us.positive?
      end
    end

    ranked = all_players.sort_by do |player|
      [
        -points_by_player[player.id],
        time_us_by_player[player.id],
        player.id
      ]
    end

    ranked.each_with_index.map do |player, index|
      {
        player_id: player.id,
        place: index + 1,
        name: player.name,
        points: points_by_player[player.id],
        winner: player.winner?
      }
    end
  end

  def start!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless lobby?
      next unless game_questions.exists?

      now = Time.current
      ends_at = next_question_timer_ends_at(from: now)
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: 0,
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        started_at: now,
        current_question_opened_at: now,
        current_question_ends_at: ends_at
      )
      current_game_question.update!(opened_at: now, timer_ends_at: ends_at)
      transitioned = true
    end

    if transitioned
      schedule_or_cancel_timer!
      broadcast_state!
    end
    transitioned
  end

  def finish!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_open?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        current_question_ends_at: nil
      )
      current_game_question&.update!(closed_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    if transitioned
      GameTimer.cancel(id)
      broadcast_state!
    end
    transitioned
  end

  def finish_if_expired!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_open?
      next unless current_question_expired?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "question_closed",
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        current_question_ends_at: nil
      )
      current_game_question&.update!(closed_at: now)
      transitioned = true
    end

    if transitioned
      GameTimer.cancel(id)
      broadcast_state!
    end
    transitioned
  end

  def next_question!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_closed? && !last_question?

      now = Time.current
      ends_at = next_question_timer_ends_at(from: now)
      update!(
        status: "question_open",
        current_question_index: current_question_index + 1,
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        current_question_opened_at: now,
        current_question_ends_at: ends_at
      )
      current_game_question.update!(opened_at: now, timer_ends_at: ends_at)
      transitioned = true
    end

    if transitioned
      schedule_or_cancel_timer!
      broadcast_state!
    end
    transitioned
  end

  def end_game!(expected_version: nil)
    transitioned = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next if version_mismatch?(expected_version)
      next unless question_closed? && last_question?

      now = Time.current
      update!(
        status: "ended",
        state_version: state_version + 1,
        ended_at: now
      )
      transitioned = true
    end

    if transitioned
      GameTimer.cancel(id)
      broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: true)
    end
    transitioned
  end

  def pick_top_winners!
    changed = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless ended?

      entries = leaderboard_entries
      winner_ids = top_winner_ids(entries, winners_count)
      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false) if changed
    changed
  end

  def draw_winners!(random: SecureRandom)
    changed = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless ended?

      entries = leaderboard_entries
      winner_ids = drawn_winner_ids(entries, winners_count, random: random)
      apply_winners!(winner_ids)
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false) if changed
    changed
  end

  def reset_winners!
    changed = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless ended?

      apply_winners!([])
      changed = true
    end

    broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false) if changed
    changed
  end

  def record_answer!(player:, game_question_id:, game_option_id:)
    received_at = Time.current
    saved_question_id = nil
    saved_option_id = nil
    expired_now = false

    transaction do
      reload
      next unless question_open?

      if current_question_expired?(at: received_at)
        expired_now = true
        next
      end

      question = current_game_question
      next unless question && question.id == game_question_id.to_i

      option = question.game_options.find_by(id: game_option_id.to_i)
      next unless option

      answered_at = [ received_at, question.opened_at ].compact.max
      upsert_answer!(player: player, question: question, option: option, answered_at: answered_at)
      saved_question_id = question.id
      saved_option_id = option.id
    end

    if saved_option_id
      broadcast_moderator_counts!
      broadcast_player_answer!(player, saved_question_id, saved_option_id)
      { ok: true, game_question_id: saved_question_id, selected_option_id: saved_option_id }
    else
      finish_if_expired! if expired_now
      { ok: false, state: player_state_for(player) }
    end
  end

  def moderator_state(join_url: nil, entries: nil)
    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    build_moderator_state(question: question, total: total, join_url: join_url, entries: entries)
  end

  def public_state
    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    build_public_state(question: question, total: total)
  end

  def player_state_for(player, entries: nil)
    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    state = build_public_state(question: question, total: total).merge(
      player_name: player.name,
      selected_option_id: nil
    )

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      selected_option_id = Answer.where(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id).pick(:game_option_id)
      state[:selected_option_id] = selected_option_id

      if question_closed?
        state[:outcome] =
          if selected_option_id.nil?
            "none"
          elsif question.game_options.any? { |opt| opt.id == selected_option_id && opt.correct? }
            "correct"
          else
            "wrong"
          end
      end
    elsif ended?
      entries ||= leaderboard_entries
      entry = entries.find { |item| item[:player_id] == player.id }
      if entry
        state[:place] = entry[:place]
        state[:total_players] = entries.size
        state[:points] = entry[:points]
        state[:winner] = entry[:winner]
      end
    end

    state
  end

  def moderator_stream_name
    "game_moderator:#{id}"
  end

  def public_stream_name
    "game_public:#{id}"
  end

  def player_stream_name(player)
    "game_player:#{id}:#{player.id}"
  end

  def broadcast_state!
    if ended?
      broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: true)
      return
    end

    question = (question_open? || question_closed?) ? current_game_question : nil
    total = total_questions_count
    pub_state = build_public_state(question: question, total: total)
    mod_state = build_moderator_state(question: question, total: total)

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(public_stream_name, pub_state)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, mod_state)
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_state!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, moderator_state)
  end

  def broadcast_ended_state!(include_public: false)
    entries = leaderboard_entries
    total_players = entries.size
    total_questions = total_questions_count
    base_public = build_public_state(question: nil, total: total_questions)
    mod_state = build_moderator_state(question: nil, total: total_questions, entries: entries)

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(moderator_stream_name, mod_state)

    entries.each do |entry|
      personal_payload = base_public.merge(
        player_name: entry[:name],
        selected_option_id: nil,
        place: entry[:place],
        total_players: total_players,
        points: entry[:points],
        winner: entry[:winner]
      )
      ActionCable.server.broadcast("game_player:#{id}:#{entry[:player_id]}", personal_payload)
    end

    ActionCable.server.broadcast(public_stream_name, base_public) if include_public
  end

  def broadcast_moderator_counts!
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      moderator_stream_name,
      {
        type: "counts",
        state_version: state_version,
        active_players_count: active_players_count,
        answers_count: current_answers_count
      }
    )
  end

  def broadcast_player_answer!(player, game_question_id, game_option_id)
    ActionCable.server.broadcast(
      player_stream_name(player),
      {
        type: "player_answer",
        game_question_id: game_question_id,
        selected_option_id: game_option_id
      }
    )
  end

  private

  def next_question_timer_ends_at(from:)
    duration = quiz.reload.timer_duration_seconds
    duration.positive? ? from + duration.seconds : nil
  end

  def schedule_or_cancel_timer!
    if question_open? && current_question_ends_at.present?
      GameTimer.schedule(id, state_version, current_question_ends_at)
    else
      GameTimer.cancel(id)
    end
  end

  def build_moderator_state(question:, total:, join_url: nil, entries: nil)
    answers_count = question ? question.answers.count : 0

    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      code: code,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      winners_count: winners_count,
      active_players_count: active_players_count,
      answers_count: answers_count,
      question_number: current_question_number,
      total_questions: total,
      last_question: current_question_index.present? && current_question_index >= total - 1,
      timer_remaining_ms: timer_remaining_ms,
      question: nil
    }
    payload[:join_url] = join_url if join_url.present?

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      option_counts = question_closed? ? question.answers.group(:game_option_id).count : {}
      total_answers = option_counts.values.sum

      payload[:question] = {
        id: question.id,
        body: question.body,
        options: question.game_options.ordered.map do |opt|
          item = {
            id: opt.id,
            position: opt.position,
            body: opt.body
          }
          if question_closed?
            count = option_counts.fetch(opt.id, 0)
            item[:correct] = opt.correct?
            item[:count] = count
            item[:share] = total_answers.positive? ? ((count * 100.0) / total_answers).round(1) : 0
          end
          item
        end
      }
    elsif ended?
      entries ||= leaderboard_entries
      payload[:leaderboard] = entries
      payload[:has_winners] = entries.any? { |entry| entry[:winner] }
    end

    payload
  end

  def build_public_state(question:, total:)
    payload = {
      type: "state",
      status: status,
      state_version: state_version,
      quiz_title: quiz.title,
      question_number: current_question_number,
      total_questions: total,
      question: nil
    }

    if question && (question_open? || question_closed?)
      payload[:question] = {
        id: question.id,
        body: question.body,
        options: question.game_options.ordered.map do |opt|
          item = {
            id: opt.id,
            position: opt.position,
            body: opt.body
          }
          # Never reveal correct options before the question is closed.
          item[:correct] = opt.correct? if question_closed?
          item
        end
      }
    end

    payload
  end

  def top_winner_ids(entries, count)
    entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }.first(count).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
  end

  def drawn_winner_ids(entries, count, random: SecureRandom)
    eligible = entries.select { |entry| entry[:points].positive? }
    return [] if eligible.empty?
    return eligible.map { |entry| entry[:player_id] } if eligible.size <= count

    cutoff_points = eligible[count - 1][:points]
    guaranteed = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] > cutoff_points }
    remaining = count - guaranteed.size
    tied_at_cutoff = eligible.select { |entry| entry[:points] == cutoff_points }
    drawn = tied_at_cutoff.sample(remaining, random: random)

    (guaranteed + drawn).map { |entry| entry[:player_id] }
  end

  def apply_winners!(winner_ids)
    players.update_all(winner: false)
    players.where(id: winner_ids).update_all(winner: true) if winner_ids.any?
    update!(state_version: state_version + 1)
  end

  def version_mismatch?(expected_version)
    expected_version.present? && state_version != expected_version.to_i
  end

  def upsert_answer!(player:, question:, option:, answered_at: Time.current)
    answer = Answer.find_or_initialize_by(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id)
    answer.game_id = id
    answer.game_option_id = option.id
    answer.answered_at = answered_at
    answer.save!
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
    existing = Answer.find_by!(player_id: player.id, game_question_id: question.id)
    existing.update!(game_option_id: option.id, answered_at: answered_at)
  end
end
EOF

class GamePlayerChannel < ApplicationCable::Channel
  def subscribed
    @game = Game.find_by(code: params[:code].to_s.upcase)
    @player = Player.find_signed(params[:token], purpose: :player_stream)
    return reject unless @game && @player && @player.game_id == @game.id

    @presence_connection_id = SecureRandom.hex(8)

    stream_from @game.public_stream_name
    stream_from @game.player_stream_name(@player)

    @presence_registered = true
    changed, _count = GamePresence.connect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    @game.reload
    @game.sync_timer!

    transmit @game.player_state_for(@player)
    @game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if changed && !@game.ended?
  end

  def unsubscribed
    return unless @presence_registered && @game && @player

    @presence_registered = false
    changed, _count = GamePresence.disconnect(@game.id, @player.id, @presence_connection_id)
    if changed
      game = Game.find_by(id: @game.id)
      game.broadcast_moderator_counts! if game && !game.ended?
    end
  end
end

First, the quiz form: looks good, clear structure with error handling, and the timer inputs are well-labeled. That `.field-row` div with its two timer inputs – I'll remember to ensure that those inner `.field` divs don't inherit extra bottom margin, that can be a subtle but annoying visual bug. And, of course, the validation behavior on the number fields: good that it preserves the user's input and displays a clear error message.

Next, the game show view. Okay, looking at the conditional rendering for the timer based on `@state[:status]`: it's all consistent. The `.stage-timer` is present only during `question_open` and appropriately absent elsewhere. Clean code. No gotchas there. And the format_timer_ms helper looks solid.

Now, the core of this review: the JavaScript controller. We're going line by line here to ensure every detail is nailed down.

1.  **Initialization and Connection:** The `connect()` method initializes all the timer state variables. A clear reset and immediate update upon connection are essential. The `syncTimerFromState` function and `updateTimerDisplay` are called immediately upon connection, which handles the initial state correctly. Good. The `disconnect` method is also clean: stops the countdown.

2.  **`applyState` Method (and State Handling):**  The version check to prevent stale state updates is critical.  Here's where it gets interesting: the `sameScreen` condition. It makes sense that we *may* need to update the timer, depending on the game state (question open or not open). If a question is open (with same id) there is a check if the timer element was rendered already. If true, and game state is "question open", then `updateCounters` and `syncTimerFromState` are called. This is all correct.
    If the question is not open or different from before, the `syncTimerFromState` function is called with `reset = true`, then the DOM is rendered (`this.render`), then the timer is updated (`this.updateTimerDisplay`).
    This also handles the case when opening a new question with timer, or transitioning from a non timed game state. The reset in this case will be called, then the timer is updated to show proper time, after it is rendered in the DOM.

3.  **`syncTimerFromState` Method (and the heart of the countdown):** This is the core logic. First, checks if the timer should be rendered or not, based on the `status`.  Then, calculates the `candidateDeadline` using `performance.now()` for accurate timing and updates if needed. The `reset` parameter is important, and the logic around the deadline update looks correct: re-calibrating if there's significant drift or a reset is requested. The `startCountdownInterval` and `stopCountdownInterval` logic, along with the calls to `updateTimerDisplay`, all seem appropriate. I notice a check for positive `remainingTimerMs` before starting the countdown - this is right, preventing negative times.

4.  **Edge Case: Timing between `syncTimerFromState` and `render`:** A key point:  the subtle dance between `syncTimerFromState` and DOM updates.  Specifically, `syncTimerFromState({ reset: true })` calls `updateTimerDisplay()` *before* the DOM is updated through `render()`. We need the old timer element (if it exists) to be replaced by the new element after we've set `lastRenderedTimerText = null` or potentially updated it. That means `updateTimerDisplay()` is run before the timer DOM element is created or updated in the `render` function. This is critical to ensure things are in sync.  This ensures no double updates. The timing and edge cases are handled correctly.

5.  **Visibility Change and Expiry Sync:** The `visibilitychange` handler is well-designed.  The `fetchState()` is triggered when the tab re-gains focus, re-calibrating the timer or transitioning the game state if the question expired. Updating the display immediately ensures a good user experience. This handles cases where the tab was hidden for a while; the server provides the true state, and the controller adjusts accordingly.

With all that said, the timer implementation looks very robust. I'm ready to write those files now, confident in the design.

require "concurrent"

class GameTimer
  Entry = Struct.new(:version, :ends_at, :task, keyword_init: true)

  class << self
    def schedule(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      return unless ends_at

      mutex.synchronize do
        cancel_locked(game_id)
        schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      end
    end

    def ensure_scheduled(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      return unless ends_at

      mutex.synchronize do
        existing = entries[game_id]
        return if existing && existing.version == expected_version && existing.task&.pending?

        cancel_locked(game_id)
        schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      end
    end

    def cancel(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        cancel_locked(game_id)
      end
    end

    def reset!
      mutex.synchronize do
        entries.each_value { |entry| entry.task&.cancel }
        entries.clear
      end
    end

    def scheduled?(game_id)
      mutex.synchronize do
        entry = entries[game_id]
        entry.present? && entry.task&.pending?
      end
    end

    def recover_open_games!
      Game.where(status: "question_open").where.not(current_question_ends_at: nil).find_each do |game|
        game.sync_timer!
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid, ActiveRecord::NoDatabaseError
      nil
    end

    private

    def mutex
      @mutex ||= Mutex.new
    end

    def entries
      @entries ||= {}
    end

    def cancel_locked(game_id)
      existing = entries.delete(game_id)
      existing&.task&.cancel
    end

    def schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
      delay = [ (ends_at - Time.current).to_f + 0.002, 0.005 ].max
      entry = Entry.new(version: expected_version, ends_at: ends_at)
      entries[game_id] = entry

      entry.task = Concurrent::ScheduledTask.execute(delay) do
        fire(game_id, expected_version, ends_at, entry)
      end
    end

    def fire(game_id, expected_version, ends_at, entry)
      if Time.current < ends_at
        mutex.synchronize do
          if entries[game_id].equal?(entry)
            schedule_locked(game_id, expected_version, ends_at)
          end
        end
        return
      end

      should_run = false
      mutex.synchronize do
        if entries[game_id].equal?(entry)
          entries.delete(game_id)
          should_run = true
        end
      end
      return unless should_run

      Rails.application.executor.wrap do
        game = Game.find_by(id: game_id)
        if game && game.question_open? && game.state_version == expected_version && game.current_question_ends_at.present?
          if Time.current < game.current_question_ends_at
            ensure_scheduled(game.id, game.state_version, game.current_question_ends_at)
          else
            game.finish_if_expired!(expected_version: expected_version)
          end
        end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger&.error("[GameTimer] Failed to expire game #{game_id}: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
      nil
    end
  end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class GameTimerTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  def create_quiz(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    quiz = Quiz.create!(
      title: "Timed Quiz",
      timer_minutes: timer_minutes,
      timer_seconds: timer_seconds
    )

    q1 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Q1?", active: true)
    q1.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Right 1", correct: true },
      { body: "Wrong 1", correct: false }
    ])

    q2 = quiz.questions.build(body: "Q2?", active: true)
    q2.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Right 2", correct: true },
      { body: "Wrong 2", correct: false }
    ])

    quiz
  end

  test "0 minutes and 0 seconds means no timer is set or scheduled" do
    quiz = create_quiz(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.start!

    assert_nil game.current_question_ends_at
    assert_nil game.current_game_question.timer_ends_at
    assert_nil game.timer_remaining_ms
    assert_nil game.moderator_state[:timer_remaining_ms]
    assert_not GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)
    assert_not game.sync_timer!
    assert game.question_open?
  end

  test "opening a timed question sets deadline, exposes timer_remaining_ms only to moderator, and never leaks to players" do
    freeze_time do
      quiz = create_quiz(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
      game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
      player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")

      assert_nil game.moderator_state[:timer_remaining_ms]

      game.start!
      expected_ends_at = Time.current + 90.seconds

      assert_in_delta expected_ends_at.to_f, game.current_question_ends_at.to_f, 0.001
      assert_in_delta expected_ends_at.to_f, game.current_game_question.timer_ends_at.to_f, 0.001
      assert_equal 90_000, game.timer_remaining_ms
      assert_equal 90_000, game.moderator_state[:timer_remaining_ms]
      assert GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)

      # Players and public state must never see timer data
      assert_not game.public_state.to_json.downcase.include?("timer")
      assert_not game.player_state_for(player).to_json.downcase.include?("timer")
    end
  end

  test "countdown progresses over time, auto-finishes at 0:00 via sync_timer!, and rejects late answers" do
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-21 12:00:00") do
      quiz = create_quiz(timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 5)
      game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
      alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")
      bob = game.players.create!(name: "Bob", client_token: "tok-b")

      game.start!
      q1 = game.current_game_question
      right_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: true)
      wrong_opt = q1.game_options.find_by!(correct: false)

      travel 2.seconds
      assert_equal 3_000, game.timer_remaining_ms
      assert_not game.sync_timer!
      assert game.question_open?

      # Alice answers before deadline
      res_alice = game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: right_opt.id)
      assert res_alice[:ok]

      # Travel to exact expiry (5 seconds elapsed)
      travel 3.seconds
      assert_equal 0, game.timer_remaining_ms
      assert game.current_question_expired?

      # Bob tries to answer right at expiry -> rejected and triggers auto-finish!
      res_bob = game.record_answer!(player: bob, game_question_id: q1.id, game_option_id: wrong_opt.id)
      assert_not res_bob[:ok]
      assert_equal "question_closed", res_bob[:state][:status]
      assert_equal "none", res_bob[:state][:outcome]

      game.reload
      assert game.question_closed?
      assert_nil game.current_question_ends_at
      assert_nil game.moderator_state[:timer_remaining_ms]
      assert_not GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)
      assert_not_nil q1.reload.closed_at
      assert_equal "correct", game.player_state_for(alice)[:outcome]
      assert_equal "none", game.player_state_for(bob)[:outcome]

      # Next question starts a fresh 5-second timer
      game.next_question!
      assert game.question_open?
      assert_equal 2, game.current_question_number
      assert_equal 5_000, game.timer_remaining_ms
      assert GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)

      # Moderator finishes Q2 early before 0:00
      travel 1.second
      assert_equal 4_000, game.timer_remaining_ms
      assert game.finish!
      assert game.question_closed?
      assert_nil game.current_question_ends_at
      assert_not GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)
    end
  end

  test "destroying quiz cancels pending timer" do
    quiz = create_quiz(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 0)
    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.start!
    assert GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)

    quiz.destroy!
    assert_not GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)
  end
end

class GameTimerRealTimeTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  self.use_transactional_tests = false

  teardown do
    GameTimer.reset!
    Game.destroy_all
    Quiz.destroy_all
  end

  test "GameTimer automatically finishes an open question in real time when the timer reaches 0:00" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Real Time Timer", timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 1)
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "Quick?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Yes", correct: true },
      { body: "No", correct: false }
    ])

    game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    game.start!
    assert game.question_open?
    assert GameTimer.scheduled?(game.id)

    deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + 3.0
    until game.reload.question_closed? || Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline
      sleep 0.05
    end

    assert game.reload.question_closed?, "Expected GameTimer to auto-finish the game at 0:00"
    assert_nil game.current_question_ends_at
    assert_not_nil game.current_game_question.closed_at
  end

  test "GameTimer.recover_open_games! re-arms open timed games and closes expired ones" do
    quiz = Quiz.create!(title: "Recovery Quiz", timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 1)
    q = quiz.questions.build(body: "Recover?", active: true)
    q.save_with_option_rows([
      { body: "Yes", correct: true },
      { body: "No", correct: false }
    ])

    expired_game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    expired_game.start!
    expired_game.update_column(:current_question_ends_at, 2.seconds.ago)

    active_game = Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)
    active_game.start!

    # Simulate process restart losing in-memory timers
    GameTimer.reset!
    assert_not GameTimer.scheduled?(active_game.id)

    GameTimer.recover_open_games!

    assert expired_game.reload.question_closed?
    assert active_game.reload.question_open?
    assert GameTimer.scheduled?(active_game.id)

    deadline = Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) + 3.0
    until active_game.reload.question_closed? || Process.clock_gettime(Process::CLOCK_MONOTONIC) > deadline
      sleep 0.05
    end
    assert active_game.reload.question_closed?
  end
end

require "test_helper"

module GameChannelTestHelper
  def create_game(winners: 3, timer_minutes: 0, timer_seconds: 0)
    quiz = Quiz.create!(
      title: "Channel Quiz",
      number_of_winners: winners,
      timer_minutes: timer_minutes,
      timer_seconds: timer_seconds

class GameModeratorChannelTest < ActionCable::Channel::TestCase
  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GameModeratorChannel

  test "requires valid signed token and transmits state including ended leaderboard" do
    game = create_game(winners: 2)

    subscribe(token: "invalid-token")
    assert subscription.rejected?

    token = game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream)
    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    assert_has_stream game.moderator_stream_name
    assert_equal "lobby", transmissions.last[:status]
    assert_equal 2, transmissions.last[:winners_count]

    unsubscribe

    alice = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "a")
    game.start!
    q = game.current_game_question
    game.record_answer!(player: alice, game_question_id: q.id, game_option_id: q.game_options.find_by!(correct: true).id)
    game.finish!
    game.end_game!
    game.pick_top_winners!

    subscribe(token: token)
    assert subscription.confirmed?
    ended_payload = transmissions.last
    assert_equal "ended", ended_payload[:status]
    assert_equal 2, ended_payload[:winners_count]
    assert_equal 1, ended_payload[:leaderboard].size
    assert_equal true, ended_payload[:leaderboard][0][:winner]
  end

  test "timed game transmits timer_remaining_ms while open and auto-closes if expired" do
    travel_to Time.zone.parse("2026-11-21 16:00:00") do
      game = create_game(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
      game.start!

      token = game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream)
      subscribe(token: token)
      assert subscription.confirmed?
      assert_equal 90_000, transmissions.last[:timer_remaining_ms]
      unsubscribe

      travel 91.seconds
      subscribe(token: token)
      assert subscription.confirmed?
      assert_equal "question_closed", transmissions.last[:status]
      assert_nil transmissions.last[:timer_remaining_ms]
    end
  end
end

  include GameChannelTestHelper
  tests GamePlayerChannel

  test "tracks presence, transmits safe player state without timer, and transmits place/points/winner after end" do
    game = create_game(timer_minutes: 1, timer_seconds: 30)
    player = game.players.create!(name: "Alice", client_token: "tok-a")
    game.start!

    subscribe(code: game.code, token: "bad")

    assert_equal 1, ended_payload[:total_players]

The WebSocket handshake will re-calibrate with the server.

## Overview

Quizzy is a Ruby on Rails 8.1 application backed by SQLite (`storage/<env>.sqlite3`), Hotwire (Turbo + Stimulus via Importmap), ActionCable (`async` adapter over WebSockets), and Propshaft for local assets. All design assets (`app/assets/stylesheets/quizzy.css`, `app/assets/fonts/Inter-latin.woff2`) and QR codes (`rqrcode` generating inline HTML5 SVG) are served locally without external network dependencies.

## Runtime & Deployment

- `bin/serve` prepares `storage/`, runs `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile`, and executes single-process Puma in the foreground bound to `0.0.0.0:$PORT` (`RAILS_ENV=production` by default, 8 threads by default; SQLite pool sized to accommodate Puma + ActionCable worker threads).
- Production runs over plain HTTP (`force_ssl = false`, `assume_ssl = false`) and accepts any `Host` header (`config.hosts.clear`). ActionCable uses `allow_same_origin_as_host = true`, accepting WebSocket upgrades from any hostname over plain HTTP.
- `GET /up` serves the unauthenticated Rails health check (`200 OK`).
- All persistent data lives under `storage/`.

## Authentication

- All moderator routes live under `/moderate` and inherit from `Moderate::BaseController`.
- `Moderate::BaseController` enforces HTTP Basic authentication against `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME` and `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD` using constant-time SHA-256 digest comparison (`ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`). Empty/missing env vars reject with `401`.
- Because browsers do not send HTTP Basic credentials to `/cable`, `GameModeratorChannel` authenticates via a cryptographic signed token (`game.signed_id(purpose: :moderator_stream, expires_in: 24.hours)`) issued by `Moderate::GamesController#show`.
- Public player routes live under `/play/:code` (`PlaysController`) and do not require moderator credentials. Players are remembered per browser via an HTTP-only signed cookie (`quizzy_client_token`, `same_site: :lax`, no `secure` flag so plain HTTP works on any host) paired with `players(game_id, client_token)`.

## Data Model

### Quiz Authoring
- `Quiz` (`quizzes`: `title`, `number_of_winners` default `3`, integer `>= 1`) `has_many :questions, dependent: :destroy`, `has_many :games, dependent: :destroy`
- `Question` (`questions`: `quiz_id`, `body`, `position`, `active`) `has_many :options, dependent: :destroy`
- `Option` (`options`: `question_id`, `body`, `correct`, `position`)

### Live Games
- `Game` (`games`: `quiz_id`, `code` unique 5-char unambiguous uppercase code, `status` in `lobby|question_open|question_closed|ended`, `current_question_index`, `state_version`, `started_at`, `current_question_opened_at`, `ended_at`).
- `GameQuestion` (`game_questions`: `game_id`, `source_question_id` informational, `body`, `position`, `opened_at`, `closed_at`). Active questions are snapshotted at `Game.start_for_quiz!(quiz)` so inactive questions are skipped and later quiz edits/deletes never break existing or historical games.
- `GameOption` (`game_options`: `game_question_id`, `source_option_id` informational, `body`, `correct`, `position`).
- `Player` (`players`: `game_id`, `name`, `client_token` unique per `game_id`, `winner` boolean default `false`).
- `Answer` (`answers`: `game_id`, `player_id`, `game_question_id`, `game_option_id`, `answered_at`, unique on `[player_id, game_question_id]`).

## Scoring, Leaderboard & Prizes

- **Scoring (`Game#leaderboard_entries`)**:
  - 1 point per correct answer (`game_options.correct = true`).
  - Ties on points are broken by lower total time of **correct** answers only, calculated in exact integer microseconds from `game_questions.opened_at` to `answers.answered_at` (the player's last pick). Wrong answers and unanswered questions contribute 0 points and 0 time.
  - Remaining ties break deterministically by `players.id`.
  - Points, place, and winner status are omitted from player payloads during `lobby`, `question_open`, and `question_closed`, and revealed only when `status == "ended"`.
- **Winner Selection (`POST /moderate/games/:id/{top_winners,draw_winners,reset_winners}`)**:
  - Players with 0 points never win. If fewer than `N` (`quiz.number_of_winners`) players have points, all players with `points > 0` win.
  - `pick_top_winners!` ("Top N"): first `N` eligible players on the leaderboard win.
  - `draw_winners!` ("Draw"): every eligible player with strictly more points than the N-th place wins; remaining prizes are drawn uniformly at random (`SecureRandom`) among eligible players with exactly the N-th place's points (ignoring speed). Each click draws fresh winners.
  - `reset_winners!` ("Reset winners"): clears `players.winner = false` for all players in the game.
  - All winner mutations run inside a single transaction, bump `state_version`, and live-broadcast updated leaderboard state to the moderator screen and personal `{ place, total_players, points, winner }` payloads to every player's phone.

## Live Game Real-Time Architecture & Conference Wi-Fi Resilience

- **Channels**:
  - `GameModeratorChannel`: streams `game_moderator:<game_id>` (full moderator state + live `counts` updates) and transmits canonical state immediately on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `GamePlayerChannel`: authenticated via `player.signed_id(purpose: :player_stream)`, streams shared `game_public:<game_id>` (single O(1) broadcast for instant simultaneous question delivery) and personal `game_player:<game_id>:<player_id>` (multi-tab answer sync + personal ended results & live winner updates), registers/unregisters active presence in `GamePresence`, and transmits personal authoritative state on subscribe/reconnect.
  - `GamePublicChannel`: used on the unjoined `/play/:code` form so visitors live-transition to `"The quiz is over"` if the game ends while the join form is open, without being counted as active players.
- **Presence (`GamePresence`)**:
  - Thread-safe in-memory registry deduplicating multiple WebSocket connections per `(game_id, player_id)`. Closing a tab/socket immediately updates `Players: N` (lobby) and `Answers: X / Y` (open question).
  - Supports short HTTP leases (`touch_http`) exclusively for fallback-polling clients when WebSockets are blocked by conference networks.
- **No Answer or Score Leakage**:
  - `Game#public_state` and `Game#player_state_for` strictly omit `correct` and `outcome` fields while `status == "question_open"`, and strictly omit `points`, `place`, `total_players`, and `winner` until `status == "ended"`.
- **Resilience**:
  - State transitions use monotonic `state_version` with `expected_version` guards to prevent accidental double-click skips.
  - Answer submissions (`POST /play/:code/answer`) record arrival timestamp before acquiring the SQLite transaction lock, are serialized per client (`player_game_controller.js`) with automatic retry on transient network/5xx errors, and reconcile on `409 Conflict` if a question closes mid-flight.
  - Stimulus controllers keep WebSocket connections and fallback polling alive on the `ended` screen so `"You won!"` updates arrive live even after transient Wi-Fi drops.

## Export & Import

- `Quiz::Exporter` (`app/models/quiz/exporter.rb`) serializes a quiz to pretty-printed JSON with **strictly** `title`, `questions` (`text`, `active`, `options` with `text`, `correct`). Live game models are intentionally excluded from export.
- `Quiz::Importer` (`app/models/quiz/importer.rb`) validates JSON syntax, types, and question rules atomically in a single transaction.

## Notes for Future Releases

- `GameQuestion#opened_at`, `GameQuestion#closed_at`, `Answer#answered_at`, and `Player#winner` are persisted to support future moderator run history and response breakdowns without schema migration friction.
- ActionCable currently uses the `async` adapter (single-process Puma). If multi-worker Puma is ever enabled, switch to `solid_cable` and back `GamePresence` with SQLite under `storage/`.
"

steps.message: Let's run a full production smoke test via `bin/serve` to verify `db:prepare`, `assets:precompile`, `GET /up`, arbitrary host headers, and live timed question expiration in production mode.
steps.reasoning_content:
**Production Smoke Test Time!**

Okay, perfect, Brakeman's clean, RuboCop is happy – no red flags. Time to really put this thing through its paces with a production smoke test. I'm going to fire up `bin/serve` using the exact environment variables we need: `RAILS_ENV=production`, a specified port (either 3000 or a test port like 3005), and those essential secrets and moderator credentials. Let's make sure everything is properly configured for the production environment.

First, the server needs to start cleanly. It needs to run `db:prepare` and `assets:precompile` successfully, then listen on `0.0.0.0` on the specified port. I'll hit `/up` with a dummy `Host` header to ensure it’s responding with a 200. This is the baseline.

Next, the functional part. I'll simulate a moderator creating a quiz via HTTP. The key here is to test the timer: a quiz with an extremely short timer of 2 seconds should create enough edge cases to expose potential problems. I need to add an active question, start the game, open the question, and confirm that the timer displays "0:02" as expected. Then, I need to verify that *after* 2.3 seconds, the server correctly closes the question, setting the question status to "question_closed". Also, I need to confirm that `GET /play/:code/state` doesn't leak the timer data, and that `GET /moderate/quizzes/:id/export` also doesn't leak the timer data. This part is critical to ensure proper behavior and data separation.

Finally, clean up. I don't want to leave any test data in the production database, so I'll make sure to delete that temporary production database. No test quizzes in `storage/production.sqlite3`! Let's get this test running now.

RAILS_ENV=production \
PORT=3000 \
SECRET_KEY_BASE="0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef" \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME="mod" \
QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD="pass" \
  bin/serve > /tmp/quizzy_prod.log 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

cleanup() {
  kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
  rm -f storage/production.sqlite3*
}
trap cleanup EXIT

for i in $(seq 1 40); do
  if curl -sf -H "Host: quizzy.conf.local" http://127.0.0.1:3000/up > /dev/null; then
    echo "Server ready on iteration $i"
    break
  fi
  sleep 0.5
done

echo "=== GET /up ==="
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" -H "Host: quizzy.conf.local" http://127.0.0.1:3000/up

echo "=== Production smoke test via Ruby Net::HTTP ==="
bundle exec ruby -r net/http -r json -r uri -e '
  def req(method, path, body: nil, auth: true, accept: "text/html", cookie: nil)
    uri = URI("http://127.0.0.1:3000#{path}")
    klass = { get: Net::HTTP::Get, post: Net::HTTP::Post, patch: Net::HTTP::Patch }[method]
    r = klass.new(uri)
    r["Host"] = "quizzy.conf.local"
    r["Accept"] = accept
    r["Cookie"] = cookie if cookie
    r.basic_auth("mod", "pass") if auth
    if body.is_a?(String)
      r["Content-Type"] = "application/json"
      r.body = body
    elsif body.is_a?(Hash)
      r.set_form_data(body)
    end
    Net::HTTP.start(uri.host, uri.port) { |http| http.request(r) }
  end

  # Fetch /moderate/quizzes/new to grab CSRF token and session cookie
  res = req(:get, "/moderate/quizzes/new")
  raise "Failed new quiz: #{res.code}" unless res.code == "200"
  raise "Missing Timer minutes label" unless res.body.include?("Timer minutes")
  raise "Missing Timer seconds label" unless res.body.include?("Timer seconds")
  cookie = res.get_fields("set-cookie")&.map { |c| c.split(";").first }&.join("; ")
  csrf = res.body[/name="authenticity_token" value="([^"]+)"/, 1]

  # Create timed quiz (0m 2s)
  res = req(:post, "/moderate/quizzes", cookie: cookie, body: {
    "authenticity_token" => csrf,
    "quiz[title]" => "Prod Timer Test",
    "quiz[number_of_winners]" => "3",
    "quiz[timer_minutes]" => "0",
    "quiz[timer_seconds]" => "2"
  })
  raise "Create quiz failed: #{res.code}" unless res.code == "302"
  quiz_path = URI(res["location"]).path
  puts "Created quiz: #{quiz_path}"

  # Verify export excludes timer
  exp = req(:get, "#{quiz_path}/export", cookie: cookie)
  raise "Export failed: #{exp.code}" unless exp.code == "200"
  raise "Export leaked timer!" if exp.body.downcase.include?("timer")
  puts "Export cleanly excludes timer"

  # Add a question
  new_q = req(:get, "#{quiz_path}/questions/new", cookie: cookie)
  q_csrf = new_q.body[/name="authenticity_token" value="([^"]+)"/, 1]
  res = req(:post, "#{quiz_path}/questions", cookie: cookie, body: {
    "authenticity_token" => q_csrf,
    "question[body]" => "Prod Q1?",
    "question[active]" => "1",
    "question[option_rows][0][body]" => "Yes",
    "question[option_rows][0][correct]" => "1",
    "question[option_rows][1][body]" => "No",
    "question[option_rows][1][correct]" => "0"
  })
  raise "Create question failed: #{res.code}" unless res.code == "302"

  # Start a game
  quiz_page = req(:get, quiz_path, cookie: cookie)
  g_csrf = quiz_page.body[/name="authenticity_token" value="([^"]+)"/, 1]
  res = req(:post, "#{quiz_path}/games", cookie: cookie, body: { "authenticity_token" => g_csrf })
  raise "Create game failed: #{res.code}" unless res.code == "303"
  game_path = URI(res["location"]).path
  puts "Started game: #{game_path}"

  # Open game page & start Q1
  game_page = req(:get, game_path, cookie: cookie)
  raise "Game show failed: #{game_page.code}" unless game_page.code == "200"
  s_csrf = game_page.body[/name="csrf-token" content="([^"]+)"/, 1]
  code = game_page.body[%r{/play/([A-Z2-9]{5})}, 1]
  raise "Missing game code" unless code

  start_res = req(:post, "#{game_path}/start", cookie: cookie, accept: "application/json",
                  body: { "authenticity_token" => s_csrf, "expected_version" => "0" })
  raise "Start failed: #{start_res.code} #{start_res.body}" unless start_res.code == "200"
  state = JSON.parse(start_res.body)
  raise "Expected question_open, got #{state}" unless state["status"] == "question_open"
  raise "Expected timer_remaining_ms ~2000, got #{state["timer_remaining_ms"]}" unless state["timer_remaining_ms"].between?(1, 2000)
  puts "Q1 opened with timer_remaining_ms=#{state["timer_remaining_ms"]}"

  # Verify public player state has NO timer
  pstate = req(:get, "/play/#{code}/state", auth: false, accept: "application/json")
  raise "Player state leaked timer: #{pstate.body}" if pstate.body.downcase.include?("timer")
  puts "Player state has no timer fields"

  # Wait 2.4s and verify server auto-finished Q1!
  sleep 2.4
  after = req(:get, "#{game_path}/state", cookie: cookie, accept: "application/json")
  after_state = JSON.parse(after.body)
  raise "Expected auto-closed after 2s, got #{after_state}" unless after_state["status"] == "question_closed"
  raise "Expected nil timer_remaining_ms after close" unless after_state["timer_remaining_ms"].nil?
  puts "Q1 automatically closed at 0:00 in production!"
'
